title: Beyond the Clock: Mood, Learning, Seeing and People

scenes.tts: Light sets the clock and the pupil. Can it also change mood and learning, apart from sleep?
scenes.visual: Title card: Beyond the Clock: Mood, Learning, Seeing and People. A gold cell with arrows to a clock, a pupil and two new question-marked targets.
scenes.narration: Light sets the clock and the pupil. Can it also change mood and learning, apart from sleep?

scenes.tts: LeGates and colleagues tested this in mice, with a T seven cycle.
scenes.caption: LeGates and colleagues tested this in mice, with a T7 cycle.
scenes.visual: Label: LeGates and colleagues, 2012. A clock face appears.
scenes.narration: LeGates and colleagues tested this in mice, with a T7 cycle.

scenes.tts: That is three and a half hours of light, then three and a half hours of dark, again and again.
scenes.visual: The clock face divides into alternating light and dark wedges of 3.5 h each. On screen: 24 / 7 ≈ 3.4 cycles per day.
scenes.narration: That is three and a half hours of light, then three and a half hours of dark, again and again.

scenes.tts: T seven mice showed depression-like behaviour. Long-term potentiation in hippocampal slices was impaired.
scenes.caption: T7 mice showed depression-like behaviour. Long-term potentiation in hippocampal slices was impaired.
scenes.visual: Two panels: a mouse behaviour icon labelled depression-like behaviour; a hippocampal slice with a smaller potentiation trace.
scenes.narration: T7 mice showed depression-like behaviour. Long-term potentiation in hippocampal slices was impaired.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking I P R G Cs did not show these changes.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking ipRGCs did not show these changes.
scenes.visual: The same panels for ipRGC-ablated mice, with normal behaviour and normal potentiation.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking ipRGCs did not show these changes.

scenes.tts: Two controls matter. Earlier work found total sleep preserved under T seven.
scenes.caption: Two controls matter. Earlier work found total sleep preserved under T7.
scenes.visual: A sleep bar labelled total sleep preserved (earlier work).
scenes.narration: Two controls matter. Earlier work found total sleep preserved under T7.

scenes.tts: And the clock stayed rhythmic, although its circadian period lengthened.
scenes.visual: A rhythm trace that keeps cycling, with a slightly longer period marked.
scenes.narration: And the clock stayed rhythmic, although its circadian period lengthened.

scenes.tts: As with any ablation, this implicates the cells, not the pigment. And a mouse assay is not a diagnosis.
scenes.visual: Two cautions on screen: cells, not pigment; mouse assay, not diagnosis.
scenes.narration: As with any ablation, this implicates the cells, not the pigment. And a mouse assay is not a diagnosis.

scenes.tts: Predict. Do the mood and learning effects run through the same output, or through different ones?
scenes.visual: The gold cell with two candidate paths drawn faintly. Question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Predict. Do the mood and learning effects run through the same output, or through different ones?

scenes.tts: Fernandez and colleagues found two routes. Cells projecting mainly to the S C N were sufficient for the learning deficits.
scenes.caption: Fernandez and colleagues found two routes. Cells projecting to the SCN were sufficient for the learning deficits.
scenes.visual: One path lights from the gold cells to the SCN, then to a learning icon; faint minor branches elsewhere, labelled minor other projections, not excluded. Label: Fernandez and colleagues, 2018.
scenes.narration: Fernandez and colleagues found two routes. Cells projecting to the SCN were sufficient for the learning deficits.

scenes.tts: A separate path, to the perihabenular region next to the habenula, carried the mood effects.
scenes.visual: A second path lights to a region beside the habenula, labelled perihabenular region (PHb), then to a mood icon.
scenes.narration: A separate path, to the perihabenular region next to the habenula, carried the mood effects.

scenes.tts: In the tested paradigms, silencing this region prevented the mood-like change. Activating it was enough to produce one.
scenes.visual: PHb dims, and the mood icon returns to normal; PHb brightens, and the mood icon changes.
scenes.narration: In the tested paradigms, silencing this region prevented the mood-like change. Activating it was enough to produce one.

scenes.tts: Whether a matching circuit exists in humans was not tested.
scenes.visual: Label: human circuit not tested.
scenes.narration: Whether a matching circuit exists in humans was not tested.

scenes.tts: A smaller story asks whether these cells help with seeing patterns. Some of them send axons to the thalamic visual relay.
scenes.visual: Axons from M5 and M6 run to the dLGN.
scenes.narration: A smaller story asks whether these cells help with seeing patterns. Some of them send axons to the thalamic visual relay.

scenes.tts: Mice without rod and cone signalling could tell a striped grating from grey. But only very coarse stripes.
scenes.visual: A striped grating beside a grey field of the same average brightness. On screen: 0.16 versus 0.55 cycles per degree in wild type.
scenes.narration: Mice without rod and cone signalling could tell a striped grating from grey. But only very coarse stripes.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking melanopsin showed deficits in contrast sensitivity. Still, this is a secondary role.
scenes.visual: A contrast-sensitivity icon with a small deficit marked. Label: secondary role.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking melanopsin showed deficits in contrast sensitivity. Still, this is a secondary role.

scenes.tts: What about people? Zaidi and colleagues studied two blind adults without functional rods or cones.
scenes.visual: Two person outlines. Label: Zaidi and colleagues, 2007; two profoundly blind adults.
scenes.narration: What about people? Zaidi and colleagues studied two blind adults without functional rods or cones.

scenes.tts: In one woman, the pupil was most sensitive near four hundred eighty nanometres, after correcting for the lens.
scenes.caption: In one woman, the pupil was most sensitive near 480 nanometres, after correcting for the lens.
scenes.visual: A pupil action spectrum with its peak at 480 nm, labelled one person.
scenes.narration: In one woman, the pupil was most sensitive near 480 nanometres, after correcting for the lens.

scenes.tts: She also detected a light above chance in a forced-choice test.
scenes.visual: A two-choice test icon with her answers above the chance line.
scenes.narration: She also detected a light above chance in a forced-choice test.

scenes.tts: In one man, light of four hundred sixty nanometres suppressed melatonin.
scenes.caption: In one man, light of 460 nanometres suppressed melatonin.
scenes.visual: A melatonin bar that shrinks under 460 nm light, labelled one person.
scenes.narration: In one man, light of 460 nanometres suppressed melatonin.

scenes.tts: Two results, from two different people. Together they are an existence proof, not a population result.
scenes.visual: The two person outlines kept apart, with the label: do not merge. Existence proof.
scenes.narration: Two results, from two different people. Together they are an existence proof, not a population result.

scenes.tts: Evening screens are a separate question. In one study, people read a bright device for about four hours, on five evenings.
scenes.visual: A tablet at maximum brightness and a printed book side by side. Label: one protocol, about 4 hours on each of 5 evenings.
scenes.narration: Evening screens are a separate question. In one study, people read a bright device for about four hours, on five evenings.

scenes.tts: Melatonin was lower than in a dim-light test, and its evening rise came later than after a printed book. But the study did not separate spectrum from brightness. The link to these cells is an inference.
scenes.visual: A melatonin bar lower after device reading, and a later melatonin onset than after print. Label: spectrum and brightness not separated; no ipRGC manipulation; link inferred.
scenes.narration: Melatonin was lower than in a dim-light test, and its evening rise came later than after a printed book. But the study did not separate spectrum from brightness. The link to these cells is an inference.

scenes.tts: The same picture helps across these mouse results. Each cell pools two light signals, and different cells reach different targets. It does not explain the image-forming subtypes, and it cannot test necessity in people.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: several gold cells, each with two inputs, sending axons to different targets: clock, pupil, learning and mood. A dashed branch to the visual relay labelled not covered by this picture.
scenes.narration: The same picture helps across these mouse results. Each cell pools two light signals, and different cells reach different targets. It does not explain the image-forming subtypes, and it cannot test necessity in people.
